identity.name: Annual Calendar
identity.one_liner: The 1996 Annual Calendar — Patek invented the complication in 1996, and the 5035J is the watch that made it accessible. The reference that started the entire annual-calendar category.

narrative.story: Patek launched the annual calendar in 1996 with the 5035. The mechanism "remembers" the length of every month except February in leap year — it needs a single correction once a year, on March 1. The 5035 was the first annual calendar in series production, and the complication has since been adopted by Rolex (Sky-Dweller 2012, via the Saros system) and Vacheron. The 5035J ran 1996-2003 before the 5146 replaced it. The annual calendar is the rare Patek complication that is both a watchmaking milestone and an everyday-wearable watch.
